verses.zh: 「耶和华―你　神领你进入要得为业之地，从你面前赶出许多国民，就是赫人、革迦撒人、亚摩利人、迦南人、比利洗人、希未人、耶布斯人，共七国的民，都比你强大。
verses.en: When the Lord your God brings you to the land that you are going to occupy and forces out many nations before you—Hittites,[NOTE:1] Girgashites,[NOTE:2] Amorites,[NOTE:3] Canaanites,[NOTE:4] Perizzites,[NOTE:5] Hivites,[NOTE:6] and Jebusites,[NOTE:7] seven[NOTE:8] nations more numerous and powerful than you—
notes: Hittites. The center of Hittite power was in Anatolia (central modern Turkey). In the Late Bronze Age (1550-1200 b.c.) they were at their zenith, establishing outposts and colonies near and far. Some elements were obviously in Canaan at the time of the Conquest (1400-1350 b.c.).

Girgashites. These cannot be ethnically identified and are unknown outside the OT. They usually appear in such lists only when the intention is to have seven groups in all (see also the note on the word “seven” later in this verse).
Amorites. Originally from the upper Euphrates region (Amurru), the Amorites appear to have migrated into Canaan beginning in 2200 b.c. or thereabouts.

Canaanites. These were the indigenous peoples of the land, going back to the beginning of recorded history (ca. 3000 b.c.). The OT identifies them as descendants of Ham (Gen 10:6), the only Hamites to have settled north and east of Egypt.
Perizzites. This is probably a subgroup of Canaanites (Gen 13:7; 34:30).

Hivites. These are usually thought to be the same as the Hurrians, a people well-known in ancient Near Eastern texts. They are likely identical to the Horites (see note on the term “Horites” in Deut 2:12).
Jebusites. These inhabited the hill country, particularly in and about Jerusalem (cf. Num 13:29; Josh 15:8; 2 Sam 5:6; 24:16).

Seven. This is an ideal number in the OT, one symbolizing fullness or completeness. Therefore, the intent of the text here is not to be precise and list all of Israel’s enemies but simply to state that Israel will have a full complement of foes to deal with. For other lists of Canaanites, some with fewer than seven peoples, see Exod 3:8; 13:5; 23:23, 28; 33:2; 34:11; Deut 20:17; Josh 3:10; 9:1; 24:11. Moreover, the “Table of Nations” (Gen 10:15-19) suggests that all of these (possibly excepting the Perizzites) were offspring of Canaan and therefore Canaanites.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神将他们交给你击杀，那时你要把他们灭绝净尽，不可与他们立约，也不可怜恤他们。
verses.en: and he[NOTE:1] delivers them over to you and you attack them, you must utterly annihilate[NOTE:2] them. Make no treaty[NOTE:3] with them and show them no mercy!
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

In the Hebrew text the infinitive absolute before the finite verb emphasizes the statement. The imperfect has an obligatory nuance here. Cf. ASV “shalt (must NRSV) utterly destroy them”; CEV “must destroy them without mercy.”
Heb “covenant” (so NASB, NRSV); TEV “alliance.”

verses.zh: 不可与他们结亲。不可将你的女儿嫁他们的儿子，也不可叫你的儿子娶他们的女儿；
verses.en: You must not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters[NOTE:1] to their sons or take their daughters for your sons,
notes: Heb “Do not give your daughter to his son.” The command (beginning at 7:1) is given in the singular form of “you” to emphasize individual responsibility. At this point, the Hebrew also switches from the plural (see previous clause) to the singular in reference to the Canaanite sons and daughters. While the principle applies to everyone in the nation, the rhetorical presentation is of an individual father making a decision about his specific child and a particular potential spouse.

verses.zh: 因为他必使你儿子转离不跟从主，去事奉别神，以致耶和华的怒气向你们发作，就速速地将你们灭绝。
verses.en: for they[NOTE:1] will turn your sons away from me to worship other gods. Then the anger of the Lord will erupt against you and he will quickly destroy you.
notes: Heb “he will,” envisioning a particular case. See note in previous verse.

verses.zh: 你们却要这样待他们：拆毁他们的祭坛，打碎他们的柱像，砍下他们的木偶，用火焚烧他们雕刻的偶像。
verses.en: Instead, this is what you must do to them: You must tear down their altars, shatter their sacred pillars,[NOTE:1] cut down their sacred Asherah poles,[NOTE:2] and burn up their idols.
notes: Sacred pillars. The Hebrew word (מַצֵּבֹת, matsevot) denotes a standing pillar, usually made of stone. Its purpose was to mark the presence of a shrine or altar thought to have been visited by deity. Though sometimes associated with pure worship of the Lord (Gen 28:18, 22; 31:13; 35:14; Exod 24:4), these pillars were usually associated with pagan cults and rituals (Exod 23:24; 34:13; Deut 12:3; 1 Kgs 14:23; 2 Kgs 17:10; Hos 3:4; 10:1; Jer 43:13).

Sacred Asherah poles. A leading deity of the Canaanite pantheon was Asherah, wife/sister of El and goddess of fertility. She was commonly worshiped at shrines in or near groves of evergreen trees, or, failing that, at places marked by wooden poles (Hebrew אֲשֵׁרִים [ʾasherim], as here). They were to be burned or cut down (Deut 12:3; 16:21; Judg 6:25, 28, 30; 2 Kgs 18:4).

verses.zh: 因为你归耶和华―你　神为圣洁的民；耶和华―你　神从地上的万民中拣选你，特作自己的子民。
verses.en: For you are a people holy[NOTE:1] to the Lord your God. He[NOTE:2] has chosen you to be his people, prized[NOTE:3] above all others on the face of the earth.
notes: That is, “set apart.”
Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

Or “treasured” (so NIV, NRSV); NLT “his own special treasure.” The Hebrew term סְגֻלָּה (segullah) describes Israel as God’s choice people, those whom he elected and who are most precious to him (cf. Exod 19:4-6; Deut 14:2; 26:18; 1 Chr 29:3; Ps 135:4; Eccl 2:8 Mal 3:17). See E. Carpenter, NIDOTTE 3:224.

verses.zh: 「耶和华专爱你们，拣选你们，并非因你们的人数多于别民，原来你们的人数在万民中是最少的。
verses.en: It is not because you were more numerous than all the other peoples that the Lord favored and chose you—for in fact you were the least numerous of all peoples.

verses.zh: 只因耶和华爱你们，又因要守他向你们列祖所起的誓，就用大能的手领你们出来，从为奴之家救赎你们脱离埃及王法老的手。
verses.en: Rather it is because of his[NOTE:1] love[NOTE:2] for you and his faithfulness to the promise[NOTE:3] he solemnly vowed[NOTE:4] to your ancestors[NOTE:5] that the Lord brought you out with great power,[NOTE:6] redeeming[NOTE:7] you from the place of slavery, from the power[NOTE:8] of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
notes: Heb “the Lord’s.” See note on “He” in 7:6.
For the verb אָהֵב (ʾahev, “to love”) as a term of choice or election, see note on the word “loved” in Deut 4:37.
Heb “oath.” This is a reference to the promises of the so-called “Abrahamic Covenant” (cf. Gen 15:13-16).
Heb “swore on oath.”
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 12, 13).
Heb “by a strong hand” (NAB similar); NLT “with such amazing power.”

Redeeming you from the place of slavery. The Hebrew verb translated “redeeming” (from the root פָּדָה, padah) has the idea of redemption by the payment of a ransom. The initial symbol of this was the Passover lamb, offered by Israel to the Lord as ransom in exchange for deliverance from bondage and death (Exod 12:1-14). Later, the firstborn sons of Israel, represented by the Levites, became the ransom (Num 3:11-13). These were all types of the redemption effected by the death of Christ who described his atoning work as “a ransom for many” (Matt 20:28; cf. 1 Pet 1:18).
Heb “hand” (so KJV, NRSV), a metaphor for power or domination.

verses.zh: 所以，你要知道耶和华―你的　神，他是　神，是信实的　神；向爱他、守他诫命的人守约，施慈爱，直到千代；
verses.en: So realize that the Lord your God is the true God,[NOTE:1] the faithful God who keeps covenant faithfully[NOTE:2] with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations,
notes: Heb “the God.” The article here expresses uniqueness; cf. TEV “is the only God”; NLT “is indeed God.”

Heb “who keeps covenant and loyalty.” The syndetic construction of בְּרִית (berit) and חֶסֶד (khesed) should be understood not as “covenant” plus “loyalty” but as an adverbial construction in which חֶסֶד (“loyalty”) modifies the verb שָׁמַר (shamar, “keeps”).

verses.zh: 向恨他的人当面报应他们，将他们灭绝。凡恨他的人必报应他们，决不迟延。
verses.en: but who pays back those who hate[NOTE:1] him as they deserve and destroys them. He will not ignore[NOTE:2] those who hate him but will repay them as they deserve!
notes: For the term “hate” as synonymous with rejection or disobedience see note on the word “reject” in Deut 5:9 (cf. NRSV “reject”).
Heb “he will not hesitate concerning.”

verses.zh: 所以，你要谨守遵行我今日所吩咐你的诫命、律例、典章。」
verses.en: So keep the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that I today am commanding you to do.

verses.zh: 「你们果然听从这些典章，谨守遵行，耶和华―你　神就必照他向你列祖所起的誓守约，施慈爱。
verses.en: If you obey these ordinances and are careful to do them, the Lord your God will faithfully keep covenant with you[NOTE:1] as he promised[NOTE:2] your ancestors.
notes: Heb “will keep with you the covenant and loyalty.” On the construction used here, see v. 9.
Heb “which he swore on oath.” The relative pronoun modifies “covenant,” so one could translate “will keep faithfully the covenant (or promise) he made on oath to your ancestors.”

verses.zh: 他必爱你，赐福与你，使你人数增多，也必在他向你列祖起誓应许给你的地上赐福与你身所生的，地所产的，并你的五谷、新酒，和油，以及牛犊、羊羔。
verses.en: He will love and bless you, and make you numerous. He will bless you with many children,[NOTE:1] with the produce of your soil, your grain, your new wine, your olive oil, the offspring of your oxen, and the young of your flocks in the land that he promised your ancestors to give you.
notes: Heb “will bless the fruit of your womb” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 你必蒙福胜过万民；你们的男女没有不能生养的，牲畜也没有不能生育的。
verses.en: You will be blessed beyond all peoples; there will be no barrenness[NOTE:1] among you or your livestock.
notes: One of the ironies about the promises to the patriarchs concerning offspring was the characteristic barrenness of the wives of the men to whom these pledges were made (cf. Gen 11:30; 25:21; 29:31). Their affliction is in each case described by the very Hebrew word used here (עֲקָרָה, ʿaqarah), an affliction that will no longer prevail in Canaan.

verses.zh: 耶和华必使一切的病症离开你；你所知道埃及各样的恶疾，他不加在你身上，只加在一切恨你的人身上。
verses.en: The Lord will protect you from all sickness, and you will not experience any of the terrible diseases that you knew in Egypt; instead he will inflict them on all those who hate you.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神所要交给你的一切人民，你要将他们除灭；你眼不可顾惜他们。你也不可事奉他们的　神，因这必成为你的网罗。
verses.en: You must destroy[NOTE:1] all the people whom the Lord your God is about to deliver over to you; you must not pity them or worship[NOTE:2] their gods, for that will be a snare to you.
notes: Heb “devour” (so NRSV); KJV, NAB, NASB “consume.” The verbal form (a perfect with vav consecutive) is understood here as having an imperatival or obligatory nuance (cf. the instructions and commands that follow). Another option is to take the statement as a continuation of the preceding conditional promises and translate “and you will destroy.”
Or “serve” (so KJV, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 「你若心里说，这些国的民比我更多，我怎能赶出他们呢？
verses.en: If you think, “These nations are more numerous than I—how can I dispossess them?”

verses.zh: 你不要惧怕他们，要牢牢记念耶和华―你　神向法老和埃及全地所行的事，
verses.en: you must not fear them. You must carefully recall[NOTE:1] what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt,
notes: Heb “recalling, you must recall.” The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute before the finite verb for emphasis. Cf. KJV, ASV “shalt well remember.”

verses.zh: 就是你亲眼所看见的大试验、神迹、奇事，和大能的手，并伸出来的膀臂，都是耶和华―你　神领你出来所用的。耶和华―你　神必照样待你所惧怕的一切人民。
verses.en: the great judgments[NOTE:1] you saw, the signs and wonders, the strength and power[NOTE:2] by which he[NOTE:3] brought you out—thus the Lord your God will do to all the people you fear.
notes: Heb “testings” (so NAB), a reference to the plagues. See note at 4:34.
Heb “the strong hand and outstretched arm.” See 4:34.
Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 并且耶和华―你　神必打发黄蜂飞到他们中间，直到那剩下而藏躲的人从你面前灭亡。
verses.en: Furthermore, the Lord your God will release hornets[NOTE:1] among them until the very last ones who hide from you[NOTE:2] perish.
notes: The meaning of the term translated “hornets” (צִרְעָה, tsirʿah) is debated. Various suggestions are “discouragement” (HALOT 1056-57 s.v.; cf. NEB, TEV, CEV “panic”; NCV “terror”) and “leprosy” (J. H. Tigay, Deuteronomy [JPSTC], 360, n. 33; cf. NRSV “the pestilence”), as well as “hornet” (BDB 864 s.v.; cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NLT). The latter seems most suitable to the verb שָׁלַח (shalakh, “send”; cf. Exod 23:28; Josh 24:12).
Heb “the remnant and those who hide themselves.”

verses.zh: 你不要因他们惊恐，因为耶和华―你　神在你们中间是大而可畏的　神。
verses.en: You must not tremble in their presence, for the Lord your God, who is present among you, is a great and awesome God.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神必将这些国的民从你面前渐渐赶出；你不可把他们速速灭尽，恐怕野地的兽多起来害你。
verses.en: He,[NOTE:1] the God who leads you, will expel the nations little by little. You will not be allowed to destroy them all at once lest the wild animals overrun you.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 7:19.

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神必将他们交给你，大大地扰乱他们，直到他们灭绝了；
verses.en: The Lord your God will give them over to you; he will throw them into a great panic[NOTE:1] until they are destroyed.
notes: Heb “he will confuse them (with) great confusion.” The verb used here means “shake, stir up” (see Ruth 1:19; 1 Sam 4:5; 1 Kgs 1:45; Ps 55:2); the accompanying cognate noun refers to confusion, unrest, havoc, or panic (1 Sam 5:9, 11; 14:20; 2 Chr 15:5; Prov 15:16; Isa 22:5; Ezek 7:7; 22:5; Amos 3:9; Zech 14:13).

verses.zh: 又要将他们的君王交在你手中，你就使他们的名从天下消灭。必无一人能在你面前站立得住，直到你将他们灭绝了。
verses.en: He will hand over their kings to you, and you will erase their very names from memory.[NOTE:1] Nobody will be able to resist you until you destroy them.
notes: Heb “you will destroy their name from under heaven” (cf. KJV); NRSV “blot out their name from under heaven.”

verses.zh: 他们雕刻的神像，你们要用火焚烧；其上的金银，你不可贪图，也不可收取，免得你因此陷入网罗；这原是耶和华―你　神所憎恶的。
verses.en: You must burn the images of their gods, but do not covet the silver and gold that covers them so much that you take it for yourself and thus become ensnared by it; for it is abhorrent[NOTE:1] to the Lord your God.
notes: The Hebrew word תּוֹעֵבָה (toʿevah, “abhorrent; detestable”) describes anything detestable to the Lord because of its innate evil or inconsistency with his own nature and character. Frequently such things (or even persons) must be condemned to annihilation (חֵרֶם, kherem) lest they become a means of polluting or contaminating others (cf. Deut 13:17; 20:17-18). See M. Grisanti, NIDOTTE 4:315.

verses.zh: 可憎的物，你不可带进家去；不然，你就成了当毁灭的，与那物一样。你要十分厌恶，十分憎嫌，因为这是当毁灭的物。」
verses.en: You must not bring any abhorrent thing into your house and thereby become an object of divine wrath[NOTE:1] along with it.[NOTE:2] You must absolutely detest[NOTE:3] and abhor it,[NOTE:4] for it is an object of divine wrath.
notes: Heb “come under the ban” (so NASB); NRSV “be set apart for destruction.” The same phrase occurs again at the end of this verse.sn The Hebrew word translated an object of divine wrath (חֵרֶם, kherem) refers to persons or things placed under God’s judgment, usually to the extent of their complete destruction. See note on the phrase “divine judgment” in Deut 2:34.
Or “like it is.”

This Hebrew verb (שָׁקַץ, shaqats) is essentially synonymous with the next verb (תָעַב, taʿav; cf. תּוֹעֵבָה, toʿevah; see note on the word “abhorrent” in v. 25), though its field of meaning is more limited to cultic abomination (cf. Lev 11:11, 13; Ps 22:25).
Heb “detesting you must detest and abhorring you must abhor.” Both verbs are preceded by a cognate infinitive absolute indicating emphasis.
